policy_title: Introduce Further Powers to Curb Disruptive Protests
stated: The Conservative Party will introduce further powers to ban face coverings, pyrotechnics, and climbing on war memorials during protests. They will also strengthen police powers to prevent protests that pose a risk of serious disorder by considering cumulative impact and banning protests outside schools.

source.quote: We will introduce further powers to ban face coverings, pyrotechnics and climbing on war memorials. We will strengthen police powers to prevent protests or marches that pose a risk of serious disorder, by allowing police to take into account the cumulative impact of protests. We will ban protests outside schools to stop mobs from intimidating teachers and children.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly restricts protest rights (a core civil liberty): banning face coverings limits anonymity/free expression in assemblies, expanding police powers to ban protests on cumulative-impact grounds constrains freedom of assembly, and location bans (outside schools) restrict where lawful protest can occur — all squarely within O9's civil-liberties scope.

Strengthening police powers to prevent protests posing a risk of serious disorder is a public-order/policing measure that bears on whether the justice and policing system manages disorder effectively — a real O5 verdict on whether the powers aid or overcomplicate legitimate crowd-safety enforcement.

Banning face coverings (bodily autonomy, privacy), expanding police powers to pre-emptively ban protests on 'cumulative impact' grounds, and prohibiting protests near schools all directly restrict freedom of expression, protest, and freedom from state coercion — the core O10 indicators.

membership_note: The policy acts directly on protest rights (O10), has a plausible discriminatory side-effect on religious minorities (O9), and its stated safety rationale earns a real O5 verdict; no other fundamentals are non-negligibly affected.
